standards.name: Minimum Information About a Simulation Experiment (MIASE)
standards.abstract: MIASE targets computational simulation experiments of mathematical models of biological systems. It specifies the minimal information needed to make a simulation experiment’s description interpretable and reproducible, covering the models themselves (and any modifications), the simulation procedures and their order, the processing of numerical results, and the description of final outputs. Published as a community perspective in PLoS Computational Biology (Waltemath et al., 2011), MIASE was produced by a multi-author community to address reproducibility and reuse of simulation work across computational biology and related fields.

classification.rationale: The source is prose guidance listing what information must be reported for simulation experiments (a reporting checklist / minimal-information guideline). The document is not presented as a field-level metadata table nor as a strict ordered procedural DAG, so it best fits the 'principle' category.

principles.principle: Declare the minimal set of information needed to make a simulation experiment available to others.
principles.evidence: MIASE describes the minimal set of information that must be provided to make the description of a simulation experiment available to others.

principles.principle: Provide the list of models to use and any modifications made to them.
principles.evidence: It includes the list of models to use and their modifications, all the simulation procedures to apply and in which order, the processing of the raw numerical results, and the description of the final output.

principles.principle: Describe all simulation procedures to apply and the order in which they are applied.
principles.evidence: It includes the list of models to use and their modifications, all the simulation procedures to apply and in which order, the processing of the raw numerical results, and the description of the final output.

principles.principle: Describe the processing of raw numerical results and the final outputs (so others can interpret reproduced outputs).
principles.evidence: It includes the list of models to use and their modifications, all the simulation procedures to apply and in which order, the processing of the raw numerical results, and the description of the final output.

principles.principle: Ensure the information provided allows reproduction of the simulation experiment.
principles.evidence: MIASE allows for the reproduction of any simulation experiment.

principles.principle: Be 'MIASE compliant' by providing all information listed in the MIASE guidelines.
principles.evidence: MIASE compliant A simulation description that provides all information listed generally by the MIASEguidelines.

standards.notes: Extraction focused on high-level reporting requirements explicitly stated in the provided PLoS Computational Biology perspective (Waltemath et al., 2011).
